We regard this position as a positive one, while still recognizing that Aristotle also wavers on this issue toward an idealist basis, or toward remnants of Platonism in his thought. When he tries to solve the basic problem of the relation between the concept and reality—that is, between the universal and the particular—he introduces a Platonic element. He argues that the soul grasps the concept intuitively after repeatedly observing particular things. Aristotle could not solve this problem because the level of knowledge in his time did not allow him to bring practical activity into the solution. The problem is solved by uncovering the dialectical relationship between the universal and the individual, as dialectical materialism later did.↩︎
